results.title: Wikipitiya
results.snippet: Wikipitiya 跳至內容 makayzaay i Wikipitiya Sakizaya Wikipitiya mahicatu, iniwtu kita haw? katayni mapulung kita misulit ku wikipitiya katinengan. kukay! hamin nu kasabelih • kakuniza a kasabelih daduducan a sapacelilan bacu Subana’ay a Pu sanu Conghwaminku a nananaman pasubana’, salatlat atu kawaw nu masakapahay a kawaw, mikantuk tu niyadu’ay nipasubana’ a talakaway. makamutideng ku Conghwaminku, nu Cincaw “Ananam a Pu” sumad hantu “Subana’ay a Pu”, tawya sasaay nida “Pakitin a Tin”, “Kalaw Subana’ a Se”, “Syanac Subana’ a Se” atu “Syakay Subana’ a Se”, nakanatalay syanace nakawaw. katukuh1926 a mihcan 3 a bulad, ku Kuming Talakawaway napatideng i Kuwangcuw, tikecay pasubana’ muelabay tu kawaw. 1927 a mihcan Conghwaminku mahecek, “Tabakiyay a Cacudadan nu Conghwaminku” muelab tu Tikecay Pasubana’ a wiyuenhuy, mala satalakaway tu a subana’ay a kaway, nay “misu”, “talakaw subana’ay”, “Tebanay Kingkiusu” a pumisakaku situngus tu nu kanatal a subana’ay a kawaw. 1928 a mihcan12 a bulad 11 a demiad Conghwaminku a talakaway patinak ‘Subana’ay a Pu sakaputlic’, muliyaw pahecek tu Subana’ay a Pu nu zingkuk nananaman, lalangawan atu sadikec subana’ a kawaw u satalakaway a kaway, namakayda kya mala tatenga’ay tu ngangan Subana’a Pu.... amiazih tu kayadahay sabeleng a nitudu nipiazih Patuduay撒奇萊雅族祝禱司 kakawsan nu Sakizaya , nakamuan a pakayzaan, Di’tu nu bayu ci kabit u kakatalawan nu tademaw, izay hansa atekak ku balucu’ niza, hina sumad, kanahatu pabeli ku bayu canacnan kakanan, uyzasa matulin ku palawacu. i nu waliyan ku eneng nu Di’tu nu bayu, u sakibayu ku kawaw, alangahay, tapuku atu demiad, u katalawan nu tademaw sa balyus, ninel u nikuwannan nu Di’tu nu bayu, uyniyaca nikakelal, mabalad atu nikasumad nu demiad, u canacanan sa masasiket tu Di’tu nu bayu. hina ta bayu ku mibutinga

results.snippet: விக்கிப்பீடியா உள்ளடக்கத்துக்குச் செல் கட்டற்ற கலைக்களஞ்சியமான விக்கிப்பீடியாவில் இருந்து. தமிழ் விக்கிப்பீடியாவிற்கு வருக, யாவரும் தொகுக்கக்கூடிய ஒரு கட்டற்ற கலைக்களஞ்சியம் . தமிழ்க் கட்டுரைகள்: 1,91,301 தமிழ் பண்பாடு வரலாறு அறிவியல் கணிதம் தொழில்நுட்பம் புவியியல் சமூகம் வலைவாசல்கள் கட்டுரைகள்: அகர வரிசை - புதியன முதற்பக்கக் கட்டுரைகள் பெலோப்பிடாசு ( Pelopidas , இறப்பு கிமு 364) என்பவர் ஒரு குறிப்பிடத்தகுந்த தீபன் அரசியல்வாதியும் தளபதியும் ஆவார். நான்காம் நூற்றாண்டின் நடுப்பகுதியில் தீபன் மேலாதிக்கத்தை நிறுவுவதில் கருவியாக இருந்தார். பெலோப்பிடாசு ஒரு புகழ்பெற்ற குடும்பத்தில் பிறந்தவர். பெரும் செல்வத்தைக் கொண்டிருந்தவராக இருந்தார். இவர் தன் நண்பர்களுக்காகவும் பொதுச் சேவைக்காகவும் பங்காற்றினார். அதே நேரத்தில் இவர் ஒரு விளையாட்டு வீரரைப்போன்ற கடினமான வாழ்க்கையை வாழ்வதில் மனநிறைவு அடைந்தார்.கிமு 384 இல், இவர் மான்டினியா முற்றுகையின் போது எசுபார்த்தன்களுக்கு ஆதரவாக அனுப்பப்பட்ட தீபன் குழுவில் பணியாற்றினார். அங்கு இவர் ஆர்க்காடியன்களால் காயப்படுத்தப்பட்டார். ஆபத்தான முறையில் காயமடைந்த இவர் எபமினோண்டாசு, அஜெசிபோலிஸ் ஆகியோரால் காப்பாற்றப்பட்டார். மேலும்... மேலும் கட்டுரைகள்... இன்றைய நாளில்... அக்டோபர் 17 : உலக வறுமை ஒழிப்பு நாள் 1604 – செருமனிய வானியலாளர் யோகான்னசு கெப்லர் விண்மீன் குழாம் ஒபியூகசில் திடீரென மீயொளிர் விண்மீன் வெடிப்பு தோன்றுவதை அவதானித்தார். 1660 – இங்கிலாந்தின் முதலாம் சார்லசு மன்னனுக்கு மரண தண்டனையை அறிவித்த ஒன்பது பேர் தூக்கிலிடப்பட்டனர். 1861 – ஆத்திரேலியா குயின்சுலாந்தில் பழங்குடிகளின் தாக்குதலில் 19 வெள்ளை இனக் குடியேறிகள் கொல்லப்பட்டனர். 1907 – மார்க்கோனி அட்லாண்டிக் நகரங்களுக்கிடையேயான தனது முதலாவது கம்பியில்லாத் தொடர்பை கனடாவின் நோவா ஸ்கோசியாவுக்கும் , அயர்லாந்துக்கும் இடையே ஏற்படுத்தினார். 1933 – ஆல்பர்ட் ஐன்ஸ்டைன் நாட்சி ஜெர்மனியில் இருந்து வெளியேறி ஐக்கிய அமெரிக்காவில் குடியேறினார். 1943 – சயாம் மரண இரயில்பாதை (படம்) (பர்மா-தாய்லாந்து தொடருந்து சேவ

results.title: Wikipidia
results.snippet: Wikipidia 跳至內容 Minkahul squw Wikipidia talam spi ru mita siliq Wikibitia na Tayal Lokah su ga? Aki ta miru Wikibitia kwara ta, mhuway! bniru sa musa naha smbbaq squliq Kyo’ikbu (教育部) hya ga pzyang balay krahu na kwara zayztywaw na kwara qu kyo’ik nya sa gakkuzit, p’unro ru saysyuwaw na mmrkyas, pklahang sa kwara zyuwaw na kyo’ik gyose. aring sa ps’rux squ Cyukamingkok ga sbahun nya kya qu kakubu sawn na chingcaw maha Kyo’ikbu la, maki sa zik nya ga kya qu Sinse Chyo, Fucukyoiksi, Semong Kyo’iksi ru Syakaykyo’iksi, mtzyuwaw sa psbah sa kyo’ik na kokka. ru mucing sa 3gat na kawas tay1926, ps’rux kya sa Kwangco lga, lhingan ’mubuy mtzyuwaw na Kyo’ikgyose Iingkay qu zyuwaw nya qani. tayhuy sa kawas tay 1927 lga psr’xun naha kya balay qu lalu na Cyukamingkok lru “Cyukamingkok Raygaku Ing” musa ’miwan lalu na snyan naha ka Kyo’ik Iingkay, yasa qu mgpzyang krahu na pcyuwagan zyuwaw na kyo’ik, yaqu “Xisyo”, “Koto Kyo’ik”, “Cyuokengkyuwsyo” ru kwara ka mlmlamu ini ptnaq na zyuwaw na kyo’ik. ryax na tay 11 sa byacing tay 12 nqu kawas tay 1928 lga skayal kya na sexu Cyukamingkok lqu “gaga pinbkgan na Kyo’ikbu”. ru ps’rxun nya kya lawzi qu maha Kyoikbu hya ga spzyangkrahu balay... mita kwara biru kin ini ptnaq na zngazyan ptasan (紋面) pzyux squliq mita LeBron James 詹皇，勒布朗·詹姆士 (LeBron Raymone James Sr., ryax tay 30 byacing na 12 kawas na 1984) hya ga senmong pgnaw mari na NBA na Amirika. LeBron hya ga pzyang baq balay praw maki' tayglaing na NBA. mrkays beh Akron, State of Ohio, na Amirika, LeBron hya ga mqwas biru sa St. Vincent–St. kawas tay 2010 wal malax Cleveland Cavaliers, ru musa sangka Miami Heat. kawas tay 2011-12 lga, yasa qu misan magal icibang sa ryax nya mqyanux. kawas tay 'nyal lga magal lawzi... mita kwara biru pzyux squliq mita Gohogo (五峰鄉) hiya ga cyan maki skura te

results.snippet: ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ, ಒಂಜಿ ಸೊತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗು ಉಂದು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯಡ್ದ್, ಒಂಜಿ ಸೊತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯಗ್ ಸ್ವಾಗತ , ಈ ಸೊತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಸೊನು ಏರ್ಲಾ ಸಂಪೊಲಿಪೊಲಿ . 33 ಸಕ್ರಿಯ ಸಂಪಾದಕೆರ್ 4,003 ಲೇಕನೊಲು ತುಳುಟು ಉಂಡು ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ತುಳು ಲಿಪಿ ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊ ತುಳುತ ಒಂಜಿ ಸೊತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ . ಈ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ದಿಂಜ ಬಾಸೆಲೆಡ್ ಉಂಡು. ಇತ್ತೆ ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊಡು ಮಾಹಿತಿ ದಿಂಜಿದಿನ ದಿಂಜ ಲೇಕನ ಪುಟೊಕುಲು ಉಂಡು. ತುಳು ಪಾತೆರುನಕುಲು ತುಳುಟು ಬರೆವೊಡು. ತುಳುನು ನನಾತ್ ಬುಳೆಪಾವೊಡು. ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊಡು ಎಡ್ಡೆ ಇಚಾರೊಲೆನ್ ಅಜತ್‍ದ್, ಗಟ್ಟಿಮುಟ್ಟುಡು ಆಯಿನಾತ್ ದಿಂಜ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೊರ್ಪುನ ಲೇಖನೊಲೆನ್ ಬರೆವೊಡುಂದು ತುಳು-ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊ ಬಯಕುಂಡು. ಇಸೇಸೊ ಸೂಚನೆ: ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊನು ಕನ್ನಡ ಲಿಪಿಡ್ ಬರೆಪುನೆ. ಬೇತೆ ಲಿಪಿಡ್ ಬರೆವೊಡ್ಚಿ.‌ ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾಹಾಪ್ರಾಣ ಅಕ್ಸರೊಲು ಬೊಡ್ಚಿ. ಅಗತ್ಯ ಇತ್ತಿನವುಲು ಮಾತ್ರ ಮಾಹಾಪ್ರಾಣ ಅಕ್ಸರೊಲೆನ್‌ ಪಾಡ್ಲೆ. ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯೊಗು ಬೋಡಾಯಿನ ಮುಕ್ಯೊ ಅನುವಾದೊ ಮಲ್ಪರ ಮೂಲು ತೂಲೆ. ಸಿಸ್ಟಮ್ ಮೆಸೇಜ್‍ ಅನುವಾದೊ ಅನುವಾದೊ ಹಕ್ಕ್‌ಲೆನ್ ಮುಲ್ಪ ದೆತೊನ್ಲೆ ಮುಕ್ಯೊ ಮೆಸೇಜ್‍ ಅನುವಾದೊ ತುಳು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಟ್ಯುಟೋರಿಯಲ್ ಸುದ್ದಿಲೆಡ್ ಪಿಲಿ ಏಸ ಮಾರ್ನೆಮಿ ಉಂದು ಇರಾನಮಾಸೆದ ಮನತಾನಿತ್ ಸುರು ಅಪುನ ಪತ್ತ್ ದಿನೊತ್ತ ಒಂಜಿ ತುಳುವೆರೆ ಪರ್ಬೊ. ಮಾರ್ನೆಮಿಡ್ ಪಿಲಿ ಏಸ (ಚಿತ್ರೊಡು) ನಡಪುಂಡು. ಸೋಣೊ ತಿಂಗೊಲುಡು ಸೋಣ ಸನಿಯಾರೊ ಉನ್ಪುನೆ ಬುಕ್ಕೊ ಸೋಣದ ಜೋಗಿ ನಲಿಕೆ ನಡಪುಂಡು. ಆಟಿ ಅಮಾಸೆ ದಾನಿ ಪುಲ್ಯಕಾಂಡೆ ಪಾಲೆ ಮರ ತ ಕೆತ್ತೆದ ಮರ್ದ್ ಪರ್ದ್ ಮೆತ್ತೆದ ಗಂಜಿ ತಿನ್ಪುನೆ ಕ್ರಮೊ. ಆಟಿಕಳೆಂಜೆ ತುಳುನಾಡ ಆಟಿದ ಇಸೇಸ ಆರಾಧನೆ ಬುಕ್ಕೊ ಆಕರ್ಷಣೆ. ಕಳೆಂಜೆ ಆಟಿದ ಮಾರಿನ್ ಗಿಡರೆರೆ ಇಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲಗ್ ಬತ್ತ್ ನಲಿತ್ ಅರಿ ತಾರಾಯಿ ಕಾಣಿಗೆ ಪಡೆದ್ ಪೋಂಡ ಇಲ್ಲಡ್ ಪೊಲಿ ಉರ್ಕರುಂಡು ಪನ್ಪಿ ನಂಬಿಕೆ. ನನಾತ್ ಇತ್ತೆದ ಸಂಗತಿಲು ಲೇಕನೊ ಸೇರಾಲೆ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಸುತ್ತಾಟೊ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ - ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು - ಶಿವಮೊಗ್ಗ - ಕೊಡಗು - ಮೈಸೂರು - ಕುಡ್ಲ ತುಳು ತುಳುನಾಡ್ - ತುಳುವೆರ್ - ತುಳು ಬಾಸೆ - ತುಳು ಸಿನೆಮಾ - ತುಳು ನಾಟಕೊಲು - ಬಿಸು ಪರ್ಬ - ಕುಡ್ಲ - ಉಡುಪಿ - ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ - ಕಾಸರಗೋಡ್ - ಆಟ - ಭೂತ ಕೋಲ - ಬಂಗಾರ್ ಪಟ್ಲೇರ್ - ನೇತ್ರಾವತಿ - ಉಳ್ಳಾಲ - ಧರ್ಮಸ್ಥಳ - ಬೊಲ್ತೆರ್ - ಒರಿಯರ್ದೊರಿ ಅಸಲ್ - ತುಳು ಜಾನಪದ ಪದ್ಯ ದೇಶೊಲು ಭಾರತ - ಯುನೈಟೆಡ್ ಕಿಂಗ್ಡಮ್ - ಚೀನಾ - ರಷ್ಯಾ - ಯು.ಎಸ್.ಎ - ಆಸ್ಟ್ರೇಲಿಯಾ - ಜರ್ಮನಿ - ಜಪಾನ್ - ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ - ಶ್ರೀಲಂಕಾ - ದಕ್

results.snippet: ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ Jump to content ᥘᥧᥐ ᥖᥤ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ ᥛᥣᥰ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ ᥞᥙ ᥖᥩᥢᥲ ᥕᥧᥱ ᥑᥣᥲ. ᥘᥭᥳ ᥙᥥᥢ ᥙᥙ ᥐᥧ ᥔᥦᥢᥴ ᥔᥛᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥖᥣᥱ ᥐᥨᥢᥰ ᥐᥧ ᥐᥨᥝᥳ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥗᥣᥒᥱ ᥞᥣᥒ ᥑᥝᥲ ᥖᥨᥭᥰ ᥘᥭᥲ ၊ ᥖᥦᥛᥲ ᥘᥭᥲ ၊ ᥓᥦᥖ ᥘᥭᥲ. ᥕᥣᥛᥰ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥙᥩᥒ ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥘᥤᥐ ᥖᥭᥰ ᥛᥤᥰ 459 ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥛᥩᥢᥰ ᥙᥪᥢᥰ ᥔᥧᥢᥱ ᥖᥨᥝ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥙᥣᥳ ᥗᥣᥳ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥙᥪᥢᥰ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥙᥳ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥔᥣᥭ ᥕᥦᥢᥳ ᥖᥨᥒᥱ ᥝᥨᥒᥰ ᥐᥨᥢᥰ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥗᥦᥐᥳ ᥑᥣᥳ ᥢᥨᥝᥱ ᥘᥨᥝᥱ ᥓᥤᥱ ᥐᥧ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥐᥧ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥐ ᥑ ᥒ ᥓ ᥔ ᥕ ᥖ ᥗ ᥘ ᥙ ᥚ ᥛ ᥜ ᥝ ᥞ ᥟ ᥠ ᥡ ᥢ ᥭ ᥘᥩᥒ ᥖᥣᥒᥰ • ᥘᥩᥒ ᥛᥨᥢᥳ ᥛᥥᥰ • ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥗᥣᥛᥴ • ᥖᥣᥒᥰ ᥓᥩᥭ ᥗᥦᥛᥴ • Guestbook ᥘᥛᥰ ᥘᥬᥰ • ᥓᥣᥛᥰ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥗᥣᥢ • ᥙᥩᥒ ᥘᥤᥐ ᥖᥒᥰ ᥔᥤᥒᥲ ᥛᥫ ᥘᥭᥳ – 14 ᥟᥩᥐᥱ ᥗᥨᥝᥱ ᥙᥣᥱ 2026 ᥙᥩᥒ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥑᥫᥐ ᥖᥩᥢᥰ ᥛᥫ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥕᥣ ᥞᥣᥢᥰ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥞᥨᥝᥰ ᥐᥛᥳ ᥛᥣᥱ ᥝᥣᥱ ᥓᥣᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥟᥧᥐ ᥐᥧᥳ ᥖᥤᥐ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥟᥧᥐ ᥐᥧᥳ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥞᥥᥖᥱ ᥞᥪᥴ ᥙᥫ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥜᥫᥐᥱ ᥞᥥᥢᥰ ᥖᥨᥭᥰ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥗᥭᥰ ᥘᥦᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥔᥤᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥱ ᥛᥤᥰ ᥘᥩᥒ ᥙᥦᥐᥱ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥐᥢ ᥝᥭᥳ. ᥘᥬᥰ ᥔᥣᥛᥴ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥕᥣᥛᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥟᥩᥢ ᥐᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥗᥭᥰ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥨᥝᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥟᥝ ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥔᥩᥒᥴ ᥑᥩᥢᥴ ᥘᥨᥒᥰ ᥓᥙᥴ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥒ, ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥔᥩᥒᥴ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥝᥭᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥓᥧᥐᥴ ᥕᥦᥐ ᥕᥥ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥨᥝᥰ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥔᥣᥒᥰ ᥘᥣᥒᥰ ᥗᥦᥢᥲ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥟᥝ ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥩᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥟᥝ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥚᥧᥱ ᥕᥤᥒᥰ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥧᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥔᥤᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥱ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥐᥩᥭᥰ ᥐᥣ ᥛᥣᥒ ᥙᥩᥐ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥕᥣᥰ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥟᥢ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥒᥱ ᥕᥨᥒᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥐᥩᥢᥰ ᥐᥫᥢ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥞᥝᥳ. ᥐᥩᥙ ᥝᥣ ᥚᥣᥱ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥑᥩᥢᥴ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥛᥨᥖᥴ ᥛᥨᥖᥴ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥗᥦᥒᥲ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥟᥝ ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥝᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥓᥧᥐᥴ ᥕᥦᥒᥱ ᥕᥥᥲ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥘᥦᥲ ᥙᥩᥭᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥕᥩᥢᥰ ᥘᥨᥒᥰ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥙᥢ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥒ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥟᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥝᥣ ᥓᥛ ᥐᥢ ᥒᥣᥭᥰ ᥖᥒᥰ ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥐᥩᥭᥰ ᥐᥣ ᥟᥢ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥓᥬ ᥐᥧ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥐᥧ ᥙᥣᥰ ᥙᥥᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥓᥫᥰ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥙᥩᥰ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥙᥣᥱ ᥘᥤᥳ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥘᥥᥝ ᥐᥢ ᥟᥝ ᥖᥤ ᥙᥩᥒᥱ ᥙᥦᥐᥱ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥐᥢ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥗᥪᥒᥴ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥨᥝᥱ ᥞᥣᥱ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥛᥦᥢ
results.text: ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ Jump to content ᥘᥧᥐ ᥖᥤ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ ᥛᥣᥰ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥑᥤᥱ ᥚᥤᥱ ᥖᥤᥱ ᥕᥣᥱ ᥞᥙ ᥖᥩᥢᥲ ᥕᥧᥱ ᥑᥣᥲ. ᥘᥭᥳ ᥙᥥᥢ ᥙᥙ ᥐᥧ ᥔᥦᥢᥴ ᥔᥛᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥖᥣᥱ ᥐᥨᥢᥰ ᥐᥧ ᥐᥨᥝᥳ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥗᥣᥒᥱ ᥞᥣᥒ ᥑᥝᥲ ᥖᥨᥭᥰ ᥘᥭᥲ ၊ ᥖᥦᥛᥲ ᥘᥭᥲ ၊ ᥓᥦᥖ ᥘᥭᥲ. ᥕᥣᥛᥰ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥙᥩᥒ ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥘᥤᥐ ᥖᥭᥰ ᥛᥤᥰ 459 ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥛᥩᥢᥰ ᥙᥪᥢᥰ ᥔᥧᥢᥱ ᥖᥨᥝ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥙᥣᥳ ᥗᥣᥳ ᥝᥤᥱ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥙᥪᥢᥰ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥙᥳ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥔᥣᥭ ᥕᥦᥢᥳ ᥖᥨᥒᥱ ᥝᥨᥒᥰ ᥐᥨᥢᥰ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥗᥦᥐᥳ ᥑᥣᥳ ᥢᥨᥝᥱ ᥘᥨᥝᥱ ᥓᥤᥱ ᥐᥧ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥐᥧ ᥙᥣᥭᥰ ᥐ ᥑ ᥒ ᥓ ᥔ ᥕ ᥖ ᥗ ᥘ ᥙ ᥚ ᥛ ᥜ ᥝ ᥞ ᥟ ᥠ ᥡ ᥢ ᥭ ᥘᥩᥒ ᥖᥣᥒᥰ • ᥘᥩᥒ ᥛᥨᥢᥳ ᥛᥥᥰ • ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥗᥣᥛᥴ • ᥖᥣᥒᥰ ᥓᥩᥭ ᥗᥦᥛᥴ • Guestbook ᥘᥛᥰ ᥘᥬᥰ • ᥓᥣᥛᥰ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥗᥣᥢ • ᥙᥩᥒ ᥘᥤᥐ ᥖᥒᥰ ᥔᥤᥒᥲ ᥛᥫ ᥘᥭᥳ – 14 ᥟᥩᥐᥱ ᥗᥨᥝᥱ ᥙᥣᥱ 2026 ᥙᥩᥒ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥑᥫᥐ ᥖᥩᥢᥰ ᥛᥫ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥕᥣ ᥞᥣᥢᥰ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥞᥨᥝᥰ ᥐᥛᥳ ᥛᥣᥱ ᥝᥣᥱ ᥓᥣᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥟᥧᥐ ᥐᥧᥳ ᥖᥤᥐ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥟᥧᥐ ᥐᥧᥳ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥞᥥᥖᥱ ᥞᥪᥴ ᥙᥫ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥜᥫᥐᥱ ᥞᥥᥢᥰ ᥖᥨᥭᥰ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥗᥭᥰ ᥘᥦᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥔᥤᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥱ ᥛᥤᥰ ᥘᥩᥒ ᥙᥦᥐᥱ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥐᥢ ᥝᥭᥳ. ᥘᥬᥰ ᥔᥣᥛᥴ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥕᥣᥛᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥟᥩᥢ ᥐᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥗᥭᥰ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥝᥱ ᥕᥨᥝᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥟᥝ ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥔᥩᥒᥴ ᥑᥩᥢᥴ ᥘᥨᥒᥰ ᥓᥙᥴ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥒ, ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥔᥩᥒᥴ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥝᥭᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥓᥧᥐᥴ ᥕᥦᥐ ᥕᥥ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥨᥝᥰ ᥖᥤᥴ ᥔᥣᥒᥰ ᥘᥣᥒᥰ ᥗᥦᥢᥲ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥟᥝ ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥙᥩᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥟᥝ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥚᥧᥱ ᥕᥤᥒᥰ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥑᥨᥙ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥧᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥔᥤᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥱ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥐᥩᥭᥰ ᥐᥣ ᥛᥣᥒ ᥙᥩᥐ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥕᥣᥰ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥟᥢ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥨᥒᥱ ᥕᥨᥒᥱ ᥟᥢ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥲ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥐᥩᥢᥰ ᥐᥫᥢ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥞᥝᥳ. ᥐᥩᥙ ᥝᥣ ᥚᥣᥱ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥑᥩᥢᥴ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥖᥛᥰ ᥛᥨᥖᥴ ᥛᥨᥖᥴ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥗᥦᥒᥲ ᥚᥣᥭᥱ ᥘᥫᥒ ᥔᥛᥳ ᥟᥝ ᥙᥣᥭ ᥖᥤᥢ ᥖᥝᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥓᥧᥐᥴ ᥕᥦᥒᥱ ᥕᥥᥲ ᥔᥥᥴ ᥘᥦᥲ ᥙᥩᥭᥱ ᥞᥨᥝᥴ ᥑᥝᥱ ᥕᥩᥢᥰ ᥘᥨᥒᥰ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥙᥢ ᥖᥤ ᥘᥒ ᥛᥥᥝᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥟᥢ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥘᥭᥲ ᥝᥣ ᥓᥛ ᥐᥢ ᥒᥣᥭᥰ ᥖᥒᥰ ᥘᥣᥭᥰ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥝᥳ. ᥐᥩᥭᥰ ᥐᥣ ᥟᥢ ᥑᥝᥴ ᥘᥒ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥓᥬ ᥐᥧ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥐᥧ ᥙᥣᥰ ᥙᥥᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥓᥫᥰ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥙᥩᥰ ᥟᥛᥱ ᥙᥤᥰ ᥖᥥᥳ ᥘᥒ ᥐᥩᥒᥱ ᥕᥩᥒᥱ ᥛᥫᥢᥴ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥛᥨᥢ ᥓᥝᥲ ᥛᥫᥒᥰ ᥛᥣᥢ ᥘᥢᥳ ᥐᥩᥭᥰ. ᥑᥣᥛᥰ ᥙᥣᥱ ᥘᥤᥳ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥘᥥᥝ ᥐᥢ ᥟᥝ ᥖᥤ ᥙᥩᥒᥱ ᥙᥦᥐᥱ ᥙᥫᥒ ᥐᥢ ᥘᥒᥱ ᥘᥭᥴ ᥘᥭᥳ ᥞᥢᥴ ᥗᥪᥒᥴ ᥝᥣ ᥘᥨᥝᥱ ᥞᥣᥱ ᥑᥨᥝᥲ ᥛᥦᥢ

results.title: వికీపీడియా
results.snippet: వికీపీడియా Jump to content వికీపీడియా నుండి వికీపీడియా కు స్వాగతం! వికీపీడియా ఎవరైనా రాయదగిన స్వేచ్ఛా విజ్ఞాన సర్వస్వము. ఇక్కడ సమాచారాన్ని వాడుకోవటమే కాదు, ఉన్న సమాచారంలో అవసరమైన మార్పుచేర్పులు చెయ్యవచ్చు, కొత్త సమాచారాన్ని చేర్చవచ్చు. ప్రస్తుతం తెలుగు వికీపీడియాలో 1,29,835 వ్యాసాలున్నాయి. పూర్తి గణాంకాలు చూడండి. ఖాతా వలన లాభాలు లాగిన్ పేజీ ఎలా తోడ్పడవచ్చు? ప్రయోగశాల సహాయ కేంద్రం రోజుకొక చిట్కా పరిచయం • అన్వేషణ • కూర్చడం • ప్రశ్నలు • సహాయము • తెలుగు టైపుచేయుట విహరణ • విశేష వ్యాసాలు • అ – ఱ సూచీ ఈ వారపు వ్యాసం రెండవ చంద్రగుప్తుడు రెండవ చంద్రగుప్తుడు (సా.శ. 375–415) గుప్త సామ్రాజ్యాన్ని అత్యున్నత స్థాయికి తీసుకెళ్లిన గొప్ప చక్రవర్తులలో ఒకడు. అతను చంద్రగుప్త విక్రమాదిత్యుడుగా ప్రసిద్ధుడు. అతని పాలన కాలం భారతదేశ స్వర్ణయుగానికి శిఖరాగ్రంగా నిలిచింది. కళ, సాహిత్యం, విజ్ఞానం, పరిపాలన రంగాల్లో పురోగతి సాధించింది. అతడు సముద్రగుప్తుని కుమారుడు. చరిత్రకారులు అతన్ని రెండవ చంద్రుగుప్తుడుగా గుర్తిస్తారు. మొదటి చంద్రగుప్తుడు అతని తాత. ఢిల్లీ ఇనుప స్తంభంపై ఉన్న శాసనంలో పేర్కొన్న రాజు చంద్రుడు, చంద్రగుప్తుడే. ఆ శాసనంలో అతని సైనిక విజయాలను పేర్కొన్నారు. సైనిక విజయాలు, వివాహ సంబంధాల ద్వారా తండ్రి సముద్రగుప్తుని రాజ్య విస్తరణ విధానాన్ని కొనసాగించాడు. చారిత్రక ఆధారాల ప్రకారం, అతను అద్భుతమైన విజయాలను సాధించాడు. సస్సానిడ్లపై విజయం, పశ్చిమ క్షాత్రపులను జయించడం, హుణులను సామంతులుగా చేసుకోవడం వాటిలో కొన్ని. రెండవ చంద్రగుప్తుడి పాలనలో, గుప్త సామ్రాజ్యం అత్యున్నత స్థాయికి చేరుకుంది, పశ్చిమాన ఆక్సస్ నది నుండి తూర్పున బెంగాల్ ప్రాంతం వరకూ, ఉత్తరాన హిమాలయాల పర్వత ప్రాంతాల నుండి దక్షిణాన నర్మదా నది వరకూ విస్తరించి ఉన్న విశాలమైన భూభాగాన్ని అతను నేరుగా పాలించాడు. రెండవ చంద్రగుప్తుడు తన ప్రభావాన్ని విస్తరించి, కదంబులతో వివాహ సంబంధం కలుపుకుని కర్ణాటకలోని కుంతల ప్రాంతాన్ని పరోక్షంగా పాలించాడు. అతని కుమార్తె ప్రభావతిని వాకాటక రాజు రెండవ రుద్రసేనునికిచ్చి పెళ్ళి చేసి సంబంధం కలుపుకున్నాడు. ఆమె 20 సంవత్సరాల సుద

results.title: Википедия — донишномаи озод
results.snippet: Википедия — донишномаи озод Ҷаҳиш ба мӯҳтаво Мавод аз Википедиа — донишномаи озод Ба Википедия хуш омадед , донишномаи озод , ки ҳама метавонанд онро вироиш кунанд . Ҷустуҷӯ дар миёни 119 324 мақола Айни ҳол дар Википедия 119 324 мақола ба забони тоҷикӣ навишта шудааст. Эҷоди мақола Роҳнамо Порталҳо Ба мо ҳамроҳ шавед Мақолаи баргузида Ибни Сино Муҷассамаи Ибни сино дар назди қароргоҳи СММ Абӯалӣ Ҳусайн ибни Абдуллоҳ ибни Сино ё Ависенна , машҳур ба Абӯалӣ Сино ( форсӣ: ابوعلى سينا ‎ ; ( 16 августи соли 980 , деҳаи Афшана наздики Бухоро — 18 июни соли 1037 , Ҳамадон ) — яке аз бузургтарин донишмандон ва пизишкони замони худ аст. Ҳамчунин ахтаршинос (астроном), кимиёшинос (химик), геолог, мантиқ, палеонтолог, риёзишинос (математик), табииётшинос (физик), шоир , равоншинос (психолог), файласуф , муаллим ва адиби бузурги форсу - тоҷик . Вай беш аз 450 рисолаи илмӣ навиштааст, ки то замони мо танҳо 240-то аз он маҳфуз мондаанд. Ин рисолаҳо тамоми соҳаҳои илмро фароҳам гирифта, хусусан, 150-тояшон дар илми фалсафа ва беш аз 40-тои дигар дар илми пизишкӣ ҳастанд. Маъруфтарин асарҳои ӯ китобҳои "Ал-Шифо" ва "Қонун" ҳастанд, ки аз бузуртарин донишномаҳои илмӣ ва фалсафии ҷаҳон буда ва дар донишгоҳҳои Аврупо то асри 19 истифода бурда шудаанд. Абӯалӣ Сино дар рушди илми тиб саҳми бениҳоят арзандае гузоштааст, ки аз таҷрибаҳои худ, илми пизишкии олими грек Гален , метафизикаи Арасту (Сино яке аз шарҳдиҳандагони асосии Арасту буд), илми пизишкии Форс , Байнаннаҳрайн ва Ҳинди қадима сарчашма гирифта, онҳоро ҳамҷоя андӯхтааст. Сино ҳамчу падари тибби замонавӣ ва фармакологияи клиникӣ ба ҳисоб меравад. Вай боз асосгузори мантиқи Синоӣ, мактаби фалсафии Синоӣ аст. results.title: วิกิพีเดีย สารานุกรมเสรี
results.snippet: วิกิพีเดีย สารานุกรมเสรี ข้ามไปเนื้อหา จากวิกิพีเดีย สารานุกรมเสรี ยินดีต้อนรับสู่ วิกิพีเดีย สารานุกรม เสรี ที่ ทุกคนแก้ไขได้ ( อธิบาย ) วิกิพีเดียภาษาไทย มี 189,062 บทความ ดัชนีคำขึ้นต้น หมวดหมู่ หน้าทั้งหมด บทความแนะนำ โลโก้อัลบั้ม ไฮบริดทีโอรี ไฮบริดทีโอรี เป็นอัลบั้มเปิดตัว ของวงดนตรี ร็อก ชาวอเมริกัน ลิงคินพาร์ก อัลบั้มนี้ออกจำหน่ายเมื่อวันที่ 24 ตุลาคม พ.ศ. 2543 โดย วอร์เนอร์บราเธอร์สเรเคิดส์ เป็นอัลบั้มที่ประสบความสำเร็จในเชิงการค้า ได้รับรางวัลแผ่นเสียงทองคำ สำหรับยอดจำหน่ายกว่า 10 ล้านชุดเฉพาะประเทศสหรัฐอเมริกาในปี พ.ศ. 2553 เข้าสู่อันดับสองใน บิลบอร์ด 200 และอยู่ในอันดับต้น ๆ ในชาร์ตอื่น ๆ ทั่วโลก โดยสามารถทะยานเข้าสู่ ท็อป 20 ของ บิลบอร์ด ได้ในสัปดาห์แรก อัลบั้มนี้ได้บันทึกที่สตูดิโอเอ็นอาร์จีเรเคิดดิงส์ ในนอร์ทฮอลลีวูด รัฐแคลิฟอร์เนีย โดยมี ดอน กิลมอร์ เป็นโปรดิวเซอร์ เนื้อหาของเพลงในอัลบั้มส่วนใหญ่เป็นเนื้อหาเกี่ยวกับปัญหาและประสบการณ์ในช่วงวัยรุ่นของนักร้องนำของวง เชสเตอร์ เบนนิงตัน ชื่ออัลบั้ม ไฮบริดทีโอรี เป็นชื่อที่หยิบยกจากชื่อเดิมของวง เนื่องจากได้เปลี่ยนชื่อวงเป็น ลิงคินพาร์ค ซึ่งชื่ออัลบั้มนี้หมายความว่า 'ทฤษฎีลูกผสม' แสดงถึงแนวคิดในการผสมผสานแนวเพลง การนำแนวเพลงหลาย ๆ แนวเพลงมารวมเข้าด้วยกัน ได้แก่ อัลเทอร์เนทีฟเมทัล นูเมทัล ป็อป ฮิปฮอป อัลเทอร์เนทีฟ และเพิ่มโปรแกรมคอมพิวเตอร์แต่งเสียง ช่วยเพิ่มรูปแบบเสียงที่มีความแปลกใหม่ ทำให้เป็นแนวเพลงที่ไม่ซ้ำแบบใคร รายชื่อบทความแนะนำ ( พ.ศ. 2568 · พ.ศ. 2569 ) – โครงการบทความแนะนำ รู้ไหมว่า... เรื่องน่าสนใจจาก บทความล่าสุดและเพิ่งปรับปรุง ของวิกิพีเดีย : ขนมบรรจุซองกวายกวายวางข้างอุปกรณ์ไวไฟ ...ในไต้หวันมีความเชื่อว่า การวางขนมบรรจุซองยี่ห้อกวายกวาย ข้างอุปกรณ์อิเล็กทรอนิกส์ (ตัวอย่างในภาพ) จะทำให้อุปกรณ์นั้นทำงานอย่างราบรื่น ...ข้อเสนอแยกความแตกต่างของ Avialae จาก Aves ของ Gauthier ได้รับการยอมรับจากนักวิจัยหลายคนในสาขาบรรพชีวินวิทยาและวิวัฒนาการของนก แม้ว่านิยามที่นำมาใช้จะไม่สอดคล้องกันก็ตาม บางครั้งนักวิจ

results.snippet: ዊኪፐድያ፣ ናጻ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ ናብ ትሕዝቶ ኪድ ካብ ዊኪፐድያ፣ ናጻ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ እንቋዕ ብደሓን መጻእኩም ናብ ዊኪፐድያ ፣ ኩሉ ሰብ ከመዓራርይ ዝኽእል ናጻ ናይ ትሕዝቶ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ። ኣብ 366 ጽሑፋት ድለይ ኣብዚ ሕጂ እዋን 366 ጽሑፋት ብ ትግርኛ ኣለዉ። ዊኪፐድያ ብትግርኛ ብ29 ለካቲት 2004 ጀሚሩ። ንዕለት ዝተሓርየ ጽሑፍ ጉግል ኣርማ ጉግል ጉግል ው.ሓ.ኩ (ውሱን ሓላፍነት ኩባንያ) (ብ እንግሊዝኛ ፦ Google LLC)፣ ናይ ኣመሪካዊ ኣልፋበት ቀንዲ መለስተኛ (subsidiary) ኩባንያ እዩ፣ ፍሉይ ክእለቱ ድማ ምስ ኢንተርነት ፣ ሶፍትዌር ፣ ኤለክትሮኒካዊ መሳርሒታትን ካልኦት ቴክኖሎጂታትን ዝተኣሳሰሩ ፍርያትን ኣገልግሎታትን እዮም። ቀንዲ ፍርያት ጉግል ተመሳሳሊ ስም ዘሎ ናይ ኢንተርነት ትሕዝቶ ምድላይ ሞተር እዩ፣ ዋላ እኳ ካልኦት ፍርያትን ኣገልግሎታትን ከምቲ ናይ ጉግል ድራይቭ (Google Drive) ቤት ጽሕፈት ተርታ ኣቕሑ፣ እቲ ጂመይል (Gmail) ዝበሃል ኢመይል ፣ ናይ ጉግል ካርታታት (Google Maps)፣ ጉግል ስትሪት ቪው ን (Google Street View) ጉግል ኤርዝ ን (Google Earth) ናይ ካርታ ኣገልግሎታቱ፣ እቲ ናይ ዩትዩብ (YouTube) ቪድዮታት መርበብ ሓበሬታን ካልኦት ናይ መርበብ ሓበሬታ ኣገልግሎታትን ከም ጉግል መጻሕፍቲ (Google Books)፣ ጉግል ዜና ን (Google News) ተርጓሚ ጉግል ን (Google Translate) የቕርብ እንተኾነ። ኣንብብ ሕጹያት ንዕለት ዝተሓርየ ምስሊ ዝርዝር ፖርታላት (መደባት) ሃገራት ስነ ፍልጠት ኤርትራ ሕሳብ ባህላዊ ፍልጠታት ጂኦግራፊ ሕብረተ ሰብ ተለቪዥን ፍልስፍና ስነ መግቢ ተክኖሎጂ ቍጠባ ስነ ጥበብን ባህልን ታሪኽ ቋንቋ ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ሃይማኖት ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ሕጊ ስነ ሂወት ስነ ጽሑፍ ቅብኣ ሕርሻ ሕግታት ተፈጥሮ ስነ ሰብ ስነ ጠፈር ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ትምህርቲ ሕክምና ሕክምና ሙዚቃ ስነ ቀመም ‎ ስነ ቀመም ስፖርት ፖለቲካ ካልኦት ፕሮጀክታት መሰረት ዊኪሜድያ ዊኪፐድያ ሓደ ካብቶም ፕሮጀክታት ዊኪሜድያ እዩ፣ ብ መሰረት ዊኪሜድያ (Wikimedia Foundation) ዝመሓደር። ዊኪሜድያ ኮመንዝ ዊኪሜድያ ኮመንዝ ምስልታትን ሕብረ-ሜድያውን ዊኪ-መዝገበ-ቃላት ዊኪ-መዝገበ-ቃላት ናጻ መዝገበ-ቃላት ዊኪዳታ ዊኪዳታ ናጻ መዋፈሪ ሓበሬታ ዊኪመጻሕፍቲ ዊኪመጻሕፍቲ መምሃሪ መጻሕፍትን መምርሒታትን ዊኪዜና ዊኪዜና ናጻ ዜና ዊኪኰውት ዊኪኰውት ጥርናፈ ጥቕስታት ዊኪሶርስ ዊኪሶርስ ናጻ ቤተ-መጻሕፍቲ ዊኪጅር ዊኪጅር መዝገብ ጅር ዊኪቨርሲቲ ዊኪቨርሲቲ መምሃሪ ሃብቲ ዊኪጉዕዞታት ዊኪጉዕዞታት ሓባሪ ጉዕዞ ሜታ-ዊኪ – ምውህሃድ ፕሮጀክታት ካብ « https://ti.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=መበገሲ_ገጽ&oldid=22535 » ተረኺቡ መደብ ፦ ዊኪፐድያ:ሞደላት መበገሲ ገጽ 349 ቋንቋታት Аԥсшәа Acèh Адыгабзэ Afrikaans Alemannisch Алтай тил አማርኛ Pangcah Aragonés Ænglisc Obolo अंगिका العربية ܐܪܡܝܐ الدارجة مصرى অসমীয়া Asturianu Atikamekw Авар Kotava अवधी Aymar aru Azərbaycanca تۆرکجه Ба
results.text: ዊኪፐድያ፣ ናጻ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ ናብ ትሕዝቶ ኪድ ካብ ዊኪፐድያ፣ ናጻ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ እንቋዕ ብደሓን መጻእኩም ናብ ዊኪፐድያ ፣ ኩሉ ሰብ ከመዓራርይ ዝኽእል ናጻ ናይ ትሕዝቶ ኢንሳይክሎፐድያ። ኣብ 366 ጽሑፋት ድለይ ኣብዚ ሕጂ እዋን 366 ጽሑፋት ብ ትግርኛ ኣለዉ። ዊኪፐድያ ብትግርኛ ብ29 ለካቲት 2004 ጀሚሩ። ንዕለት ዝተሓርየ ጽሑፍ ጉግል ኣርማ ጉግል ጉግል ው.ሓ.ኩ (ውሱን ሓላፍነት ኩባንያ) (ብ እንግሊዝኛ ፦ Google LLC)፣ ናይ ኣመሪካዊ ኣልፋበት ቀንዲ መለስተኛ (subsidiary) ኩባንያ እዩ፣ ፍሉይ ክእለቱ ድማ ምስ ኢንተርነት ፣ ሶፍትዌር ፣ ኤለክትሮኒካዊ መሳርሒታትን ካልኦት ቴክኖሎጂታትን ዝተኣሳሰሩ ፍርያትን ኣገልግሎታትን እዮም። ቀንዲ ፍርያት ጉግል ተመሳሳሊ ስም ዘሎ ናይ ኢንተርነት ትሕዝቶ ምድላይ ሞተር እዩ፣ ዋላ እኳ ካልኦት ፍርያትን ኣገልግሎታትን ከምቲ ናይ ጉግል ድራይቭ (Google Drive) ቤት ጽሕፈት ተርታ ኣቕሑ፣ እቲ ጂመይል (Gmail) ዝበሃል ኢመይል ፣ ናይ ጉግል ካርታታት (Google Maps)፣ ጉግል ስትሪት ቪው ን (Google Street View) ጉግል ኤርዝ ን (Google Earth) ናይ ካርታ ኣገልግሎታቱ፣ እቲ ናይ ዩትዩብ (YouTube) ቪድዮታት መርበብ ሓበሬታን ካልኦት ናይ መርበብ ሓበሬታ ኣገልግሎታትን ከም ጉግል መጻሕፍቲ (Google Books)፣ ጉግል ዜና ን (Google News) ተርጓሚ ጉግል ን (Google Translate) የቕርብ እንተኾነ። ኣንብብ ሕጹያት ንዕለት ዝተሓርየ ምስሊ ዝርዝር ፖርታላት (መደባት) ሃገራት ስነ ፍልጠት ኤርትራ ሕሳብ ባህላዊ ፍልጠታት ጂኦግራፊ ሕብረተ ሰብ ተለቪዥን ፍልስፍና ስነ መግቢ ተክኖሎጂ ቍጠባ ስነ ጥበብን ባህልን ታሪኽ ቋንቋ ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ሃይማኖት ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ሕጊ ስነ ሂወት ስነ ጽሑፍ ቅብኣ ሕርሻ ሕግታት ተፈጥሮ ስነ ሰብ ስነ ጠፈር ማዕጾ:ሕብረተ ሰብ ትምህርቲ ሕክምና ሕክምና ሙዚቃ ስነ ቀመም ‎ ስነ ቀመም ስፖርት ፖለቲካ ካልኦት ፕሮጀክታት መሰረት ዊኪሜድያ ዊኪፐድያ ሓደ ካብቶም ፕሮጀክታት ዊኪሜድያ እዩ፣ ብ መሰረት ዊኪሜድያ (Wikimedia Foundation) ዝመሓደር። ዊኪሜድያ ኮመንዝ ዊኪሜድያ ኮመንዝ ምስልታትን ሕብረ-ሜድያውን ዊኪ-መዝገበ-ቃላት ዊኪ-መዝገበ-ቃላት ናጻ መዝገበ-ቃላት ዊኪዳታ ዊኪዳታ ናጻ መዋፈሪ ሓበሬታ ዊኪመጻሕፍቲ ዊኪመጻሕፍቲ መምሃሪ መጻሕፍትን መምርሒታትን ዊኪዜና ዊኪዜና ናጻ ዜና ዊኪኰውት ዊኪኰውት ጥርናፈ ጥቕስታት ዊኪሶርስ ዊኪሶርስ ናጻ ቤተ-መጻሕፍቲ ዊኪጅር ዊኪጅር መዝገብ ጅር ዊኪቨርሲቲ ዊኪቨርሲቲ መምሃሪ ሃብቲ ዊኪጉዕዞታት ዊኪጉዕዞታት ሓባሪ ጉዕዞ ሜታ-ዊኪ – ምውህሃድ ፕሮጀክታት ካብ « https://ti.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=መበገሲ_ገጽ&oldid=22535 » ተረኺቡ መደብ ፦ ዊኪፐድያ:ሞደላት መበገሲ ገጽ 349 ቋንቋታት Аԥсшәа Acèh Адыгабзэ Afrikaans Alemannisch Алтай тил አማርኛ Pangcah Aragonés Ænglisc Obolo अंगिका العربية ܐܪܡܝܐ الدارجة مصرى অসমীয়া Asturianu Atikamekw Авар Kotava अवधी Aymar aru Azərbaycanca تۆرکجه Ба

results.snippet: ዊኪፒድያ አስክ ጸብጥ ተዐዴ ምን ዊኪፒድያ መርሐበ ብኩም እት ዊኪፒድያ ህግየ ትግሬ፡ ለገብአ ምንኩም እግል-ለአስንዮ ለቀድር ሑር ኤንሳይክሉፒድያ! ዐድነ ነኣምር ኣሳር ወስያሐት ፈን ወዓዳት ስያሰት አክትበት ዕሉም ወቴክኖሎጂ ታሪክ ዓፍየት ታሪክ ሐያት ሕበርበሮ ርያደት ህርከክ መራጄዕ ህግያ ትግሬ ብለዕ ወስታይ ርክን ስወር መንታይ ዊኪፒድያ ላቱ መሻርዕ ኮመንስ ሚድያዊኪ ዊኪሚድያ ዊኪቡክስ ዊኪደታ ዊኪኒዩስ ዊኪኮት ዊኪሶርስ ዊኪመድያ ዊኪቨርሲቲ ዊኪቮያጅ ዊክሸነሪ ምን " https://tig.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=አግዳ_ገጽ&oldid=8461 " ጀለበ 349 ሀገጊት Аԥсшәа Acèh Адыгабзэ Afrikaans Alemannisch Алтай тил አማርኛ Pangcah Aragonés Ænglisc Obolo अंगिका العربية ܐܪܡܝܐ الدارجة مصرى অসমীয়া Asturianu Atikamekw Авар Kotava अवधी Aymar aru Azərbaycanca تۆرکجه Башҡортса Basa Bali Boarisch Žemaitėška Batak Toba Bikol Central Bajau Sama Беларуская (тарашкевіца) Беларуская Betawi Български भोजपुरी Bislama Banjar ပအိုဝ်ႏဘာႏသာႏ Bamanankan বাংলা བོད་ཡིག Bòo pìkkà বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া মণিপুরী Brezhoneg Bosanski Batak Mandailing Basa Ugi Буряад Català Chavacano de Zamboanga 閩東語 / Mìng-dĕ̤ng-ngṳ̄ Нохчийн Cebuano Chamoru ᏣᎳᎩ Tsetsêhestâhese کوردی Corsu Nēhiyawēwin / ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐍᐏᐣ Qırımtatarca Čeština Kaszëbsczi Словѣньскъ / ⰔⰎⰑⰂⰡⰐⰠⰔⰍⰟ Чӑвашла Cymraeg Dansk Dagbanli Deutsch Dagaare Thuɔŋjäŋ Zazaki Dolnoserbski Kadazandusun डोटेली ދިވެހިބަސް ཇོང་ཁ Eʋegbe Ελληνικά Emiliàn e rumagnòl English Esperanto Español Eesti Euskara Estremeñu فارسی Mfantse Fulfulde Suomi Võro Na Vosa Vakaviti Føroyskt Fɔ̀ngbè Français Arpetan Nordfriisk Furlan Frysk Gaeilge Gagauz 贛語 Kriyòl gwiyannen Gàidhlig Galego گیلکی Avañe'ẽ गोंयची कोंकणी / Gõychi Konknni Bahasa Hulontalo 𐌲𐌿𐍄𐌹𐍃𐌺 Ghanaian Pidgin ગુજરાતી Wayuunaiki Farefare Gungbe Gaelg Hausa 客家語 / Hak-kâ-ngî Hawaiʻi עברית हिन्दी Fiji Hindi Hrvatski Hornjoserbsce Kreyòl ayisyen Magyar Հայերեն Արեւմտահայերէն Interlingua Jaku Iban Bahasa Indonesia Interlingue Igbo Igala Iñupiatun Ilokano ГӀалгӀай Ido Íslenska Medžuslovjansky Italiano ᐃᓄᒃᑎᑐᑦ / inuktitut 日本語 Patois L

Si Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck ( Dzongkha : འཇིགས་མེད་གེ་སར་རྣམ་རྒྱལ་དབང་ཕྱུག་ , Wylie: jigs med ge sar rnam rgyal dbang phyug ; ipinanganak noong Pebrero 21, 1980) ay ang ikalimang Druk Gyalpo (Dzongkha: Haring Dragon) ng Kaharian ng Bhutan at puno ng Angkan ng Wangchuck (dinastiyang Wangchuck). Siya ang kasalukuyang pinakabatang monarka at puno ng estado . Naluklok siya sa trono noong Disyembre 6, 2006 matapos magbitiw ang kanyang ama, ang ikaapat at dating Haring Dragon ng Bhutan na si Jigme Singye Wangchuck. Naganap ang pampublikong seremonya ng koronasyon noong Nobyembre 6, 2008, ang taon na minarkahan ang ika-100 ng monarkiya ng Bhutan. Kaugnay ng pamilya, panganay si Khesar ng kanyang ama at ng ikatlong asawa ng kanyang ama na si Reynang (Ashi) Tshering Yangdon. Mayroon siyang mga nakababatang kapatid na babae at lalaki, gayundin, may apat na kapatid na babae sa labas at tatlong kapatid na lalaki sa labas. Asawa niya si Jestun Pema, ang Druk Gyaltsuen (Dzongkha: Reynang Dragon) ng Bhutan. Mayroon silang dalawang anak, ang mga prinsipeng sina Jigme Namgyel Wangchuck at Jigme Ugyen Wangchuck. Pagkatapos tapusin ang kanyang pag-aaral sa mababa at mataas na paaralan sa Bhutan, nag-aral si Khesar sa ibang bansa sa Akademiyang Phillips (Andover), Akademiyang Cushing at Dalubhasaang Wheaton sa Massachusetts , Mga Nagkakaisang Estado , bago magtapos sa Dalubhasaang Magdalen, Pamantasan ng Oxford, Mga Nagkakaisa

results.title: Vikipedija
results.snippet: Vikipedija Bə mətni dəvarde Сy Vikipedija Xəš oməjon bə Vikipedija , sərbəstə ensiklopedijə kom harki bəzyne sərost kardej. Ysət Tolyšə zyvonədə 10,225 məǧolə heste. 13 Oktjabr 2026 , Sešambə Haftə vyžnijə nyvyštəj Bekəǧə Mirsalajev Mirsalajev Bekəǧə Əbulfəti zoə (22 janvar 1893 sor, Rəzgov di, Zuvandi rəjon, Lankoni ǧəzo, Urusijəti imperijə — 8 janvar 1938 sor, Azərbojčoni SSR) — tolyšə ičtimoi-sijosijə xodim, Kommunistə partijə (bolševikon) Zakavkazə Kraj komitə dyminə kotib. 1906 sorədə əcəj 13 sinənədə əcəj xyjzon bə Boku ovašte. Əǧylətijədə nati gyrdə kardə vyronədə yštə ko bino kardyše. Ko karde vaxtonədə əv yštə zynəjonən, yštə təhsiliən səjdəbe. Sabuncijədə 3-sinifə məktəbi oryxniše. 1918 sorədə bə yštə di Rəzgov ogarde u əjo Mistani dij čəmjəti šurədə kotib ko kardyše. Pešo əcəj xyjzon bə Lankon ovašte. Myǧon-Šurə Respublikə Myǧon-Šurə Respublikə elon kardejədə əv aktiv rolyš byə. Cy Respublikə Məholi Šurə Jol gyləj partizanə ǧysmi jol - Lankon ədə inǧylobə usjonədə ištirokəkə David Cirkin vyžnijə byəbe, u əcəj myovini vyrədə Širəli Axundov be. Bolševikon dylədə be-be Bekəǧə bə yštə divoži abrek Junus Abbasovi dastə nydəše, əmma cy tolyšə syə partizani Bala Məmmədi dastədə be u pešo kejnə Junus bə šurə tərəf ovašte, Bekəǧə bə əcəj dastə umžən be. Myǧon-Šurə Respublikə soxte bəpeštə, Širəli Axundov xəjli gəp žəjdə de tolyšə abreki Junus Abbasovi (Junus Rəzgovyži) u əv de Bekəǧə Mirsalajevi dastəki zynejdə əj bə šurə tərəfi okyrnije. Junusi cy "Zyvandi ucastok" komissar təjin kardejdən. Ofəjevonəti Bekəǧə bo məktobon dutejro, təhsili səvijə rost kardejro, čyvonon bə ədəbijoti u nəčiməsənəti sahə sədo kardejro, tolyšə zyvoni ozavaijero xəjli dast-pocə kardejdəbe Lankoni rəjonədə. 21 janvar 1931 soriku de Bekəǧə Mirasalajevi redaktorəti u Muzəffər Nəsirlo kotibəti

results.snippet: The MDN Web Docs site provides information about Open Web technologies including HTML, CSS, and APIs for both Web sites and progressive web apps.
results.text: MDN Web Docs Skip to main content Skip to search Resources for Developers, by Developers Documenting CSS , HTML , and JavaScript , since 2005. Featured articles Blog Celebrating 20 years of MDN MDN turns 20! Let's look at how we started, how MDN became the most trusted resource for web developers, the impact it's had on the open web, and yes, there's cake, too. Web APIs Navigation API The Navigation API provides the ability to initiate, intercept, and manage browser navigation actions. It can also examine an application's history entries. This is a successor to previous web platform features such as the History API and window.location, which solves their shortcomings and is specifically aimed at the needs of single-page applications (SPAs). Web APIs Trusted Types API The Trusted Types API gives web developers a way to ensure that input has been passed through a user-specified transformation function before being passed to an API that might execute that input. This can help to protect against client-side cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Most commonly the transformation function sanitizes the input. CSS Using CSS anchor positioning The CSS anchor positioning module defines features that allow you to tether elements together. Elements can be defined as anchor elements and anchor-positioned elements. Anchor-positioned elements can be bound to anchor elements. The anchor-positioned elements can then have their size and position set relative to the size and location of the anchor elements to which they are bound. If not then we presume you will be looking for information about why and how to get started with Python. Fortunately an experienced programmer in any programming language (whatever it may be) can pick up Python very quickly. It's also easy for beginners to use and learn, so jump in ! Installing Installing Python is generally easy, and nowadays many Linux and UNIX distributions include a recent Python. Even some Windows computers (notably those from HP) now come with Python already installed. If you do need to install Python and aren't confident about the task you can find a few notes on the BeginnersGuide/Download wiki page, but installation is unremarkable on most platforms. Learning Before getting started, you may want to find out which IDEs and text editors are tailored to make Python editing easy, browse the list of introductory books , or look at code samples that you might find helpful. There is a list of tutorials suitable for experienced programmers on the BeginnersGuide/Tutorials page. There is also a list of resources in other languages which might be useful if English is not your first language. The online documentation is your first port of call for definitive information. There is a fairly brief tutorial that gives you basic information about the language and gets you started. You can follow this by looking at the library reference for a full description of Python's many libraries and the language reference for a complete (though somewhat dry) explanation of Python's syntax. There’s plenty still to come in Python 3.16, but its first alpha is ready to try! Python 3.16.0a1 is the first of seven planned alpha releases. During the alpha phase, features may be added up until the start of the beta phase (May 4, 2027) and, if necessary, may be modified or deleted up until the release candidate phase (July 27, 2027). The final release is planned for October 5, 2027. Please keep in mind that this is a preview release and its use is not recommended for production environments. See What’s new in Python 3.16 for changes so far. (Hey, fellow core team member, if there’s a feature you’d like highlighted in a future announcement, let Savannah know .) If you maintain a library or application, please try it with this alpha and let us know how it goes. Please report Python bugs on the CPython issue tracker . The next alpha, Python 3.16.0a2, is scheduled for November 10, 2026. The full schedule is in PEP 826 . Introduction At Gretel.ai, our mission is to make it fast and easy for developers and data scientists to create production-grade synthetic data. To achieve this, we’ve designed a series of APIs that allow anyone to get up and running within minutes so they can identify, transform and generate the data necessary to fuel the testing of modern software applications and AI/ML models. Python is the engine that powers much of Gretel’s research, development, and deployment of our APIs and toolkit. From a user experience perspective, Python’s extensive libraries and frameworks (e.g., Scikit-learn and TensorFlow for machine learning, Spacy for text processing, and Numpy for data exploration), its ability to handle complex data structures, and its turnkey integrations help us ensure Gretel’s platform is easy to use and extensible to any workflow or project. results.title: Welcome to Pyramid, a Python Web Framework
results.snippet: Pyramid is a lightweight Python web framework aimed at taking small web apps into big web apps. This site provides an easy entry point into Pyramid.
results.text: Welcome to Pyramid, a Python Web Framework Pyramid The Start Small , Finish Big Stay Finished Framework Projects with ambition start small but finish big and must stay finished . You need a Python web framework that supports your decisions , by artisans for artisans . Quick Start from wsgiref.simple_server import make_server from pyramid.config import Configurator from pyramid.response import Response def hello_world(request): return Response('Hello World!') if __name__ == '__main__': with Configurator() as config: config.add_route('hello', '/') config.add_view(hello_world, route_name='hello') app = config.make_wsgi_app() server = make_server('0.0.0.0', 6543, app) server.serve_forever() Pyramid makes it easy to write web applications. You can start small with this "hello world" minimal request/response web app. This may take you far, especially while learning. As your application grows, Pyramid offers many features that make writing complex software take less effort. Pyramid works in all supported versions of Python. Our installation instructions will help you get Pyramid up and running. Pyramid's quick tutorial will take you step by step through writing a single file application, forms, database integration, and authentication. Developers may dive in to Pyramid's narrative documentation , or browse the extensive API reference . Pyramid has a rich pool of helpful resources from which to draw. Extending Pyramid is a curated and filterable list of add-ons, packages, and applications built to work with Pyramid. When You Need Pyramid Megaframeworks make decisions for you. But if you don't fit their viewpoint, you end up fighting their decisions. Microframeworks force no decisions, making it easy to start. But as your application grows, you're on your own. results.snippet: Tkinter - Wikipedia Jump to content From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Python binding to the Tk GUI toolkit Tkinter The IDLE Python editor License Python license Website https://docs.python.org/3/library/tkinter.html Tkinter is a binding to the Tk GUI toolkit for Python . It is the standard Python interface to the Tk GUI toolkit, [ 1 ] and is Python's de facto standard GUI. [ 2 ] Tkinter is included with standard Linux , Microsoft Windows and macOS installs of Python. The name Tkinter comes from Tk interface . Tkinter was written by Steen Lumholt and Guido van Rossum , [ 3 ] then later revised by Fredrik Lundh. [ 4 ] Tkinter is free software released under a Python license . [ 5 ] Description [ edit ] As with most other modern Tk bindings, Tkinter is implemented as a Python wrapper around a complete Tcl interpreter embedded in the Python interpreter . Tkinter calls are translated into Tcl commands, which are fed to this embedded interpreter, thus making it possible to mix Python and Tcl in a single application. The official Python release uses Tcl/Tk 8.6 (rather than the more up-to-date 9.0). [ 6 ] There are several popular GUI library alternatives available, such as Kivy , Pygame , Pyglet , PyGObject , PyQt , PySide , and wxPython . results.title: Riverbank Computing | Introduction
results.snippet: Riverbank Computing | Introduction What is PyQt? PyQt is a set of Python bindings for The Qt Company's Qt application framework. The bindings are implemented as a set of Python modules and contain over 1,000 classes. PyQt6 supports Qt6 and runs on Windows (Intel and ARM), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux (Intel and ARM). PyQt5 supports Qt5 and runs on Windows (Intel), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), Android, iOS and Linux (Intel). PyQt4 supports Qt v4 but both are no longer supported and no new releases will be made. License PyQt is dual licensed on all supported platforms under the GNU GPL v3 and the Riverbank Commercial License. Unlike Qt, PyQt is not available under the LGPL. You can purchase the commercial version of PyQt here . More information about licensing can be found in the License FAQ . PyQt does not include a copy of Qt. You must obtain a correctly licensed copy of Qt yourself. However, binary wheels of the GPL version of PyQt6 and PyQt5 are provided and these include a copy of the corresponding LGPL version of Qt. PyQt Components A description of the components of PyQt5 can be found in the PyQt5 Reference Guide . A description of the components of PyQt4 can be found in the PyQt4 Reference Guide . Why PyQt? PyQt brings together the Qt C++ cross-platform application framework and the cross-platform interpreted language Python . Qt is more than a GUI toolkit. It includes abstractions of network sockets, threads, Unicode, regular expressions, SQL databases, SVG, OpenGL, XML, a fully functional web browser, a help system, a multimedia framework, as well as a rich collection of GUI widgets. The Qt for Python project aims to provide a complete port of the PySide module to Qt. The development started on GitHub in May 2015. The project managed to port PySide to Qt 5.3, 5.4 & 5.5. During April 2016 The Qt Company decided to properly support the port (see details ). The module was released mid June 2018 as a Technical Preview (supporting Qt 5.11), and it was officially released without the Technical Preview tag, in December 2018 for Qt 5.12. In December 2020, the module was released for Qt6, which is the latest available version, which has the following differences: It doesn't support Python 2.7, Check the Compatibility Matrix for the supported Python version per each PySide version. This wiki page tracks the progress of the Qt for Python project development and provides further information concerning the effort. Qt for Python is available under LGPLv3 / GPLv2 and commercial license for the following platforms: Linux macOS Windows Android iOS WebAssembly amd64 aarch64 Apple Silicon 64bit arm64 armv8 arm64 (simulator, device) x86_64 (simulator) - Python 3.10+ Please notice i386/32bit architecture is not supported. Get PySide6 via pip by running: pip install pyside6 What does it look like? Code Application import sys from PySide6.QtCore import Qt from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication , QLabel if __name__ == "__main__" : app = QApplication ( sys . argv ) label = QLabel ( "Hello World" , alignment = Qt . Alignment . AlignCenter ) label . show () sys . exit ( app . exec ()) More examples can be found in the project's repository inside the examples directory. Python

results.text: Dear PyGui’s Documentation — Dear PyGui documentation » Dear PyGui’s Documentation View page source Dear PyGui’s Documentation ¶ About DPG ¶ Dear PyGui is an easy-to-use, dynamic, GPU-Accelerated, cross-platform graphical user interface toolkit(GUI) for Python. It is “built with” Dear ImGui . Features include traditional GUI elements such as buttons, radio buttons, menus and various methods to create a functional layout. Additionally, DPG has an incredible assortment of dynamic plots, tables, drawings, debugger, and multiple resource viewers. DPG is well suited for creating simple user interfaces as well as developing complex and demanding graphical interfaces. DPG offers a solid framework for developing scientific, engineering, gaming, data science and other applications that require fast and interactive interfaces. Quick Start ¶ If you’re ready to start using DPG visit the First Steps in tutorials. The Tutorials will provide a great overview and links to each topic in the API Reference for more detailed reading. However, use the API reference for the most detailed documentation on any specific topic. results.text: SciPy SciPy Fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python Get started SciPy 1.18.1 released! 2026-08-21 Fundamental algorithms SciPy provides algorithms for optimization, integration, interpolation, eigenvalue problems, algebraic equations, differential equations, statistics and many other classes of problems. Broadly applicable The algorithms and data structures provided by SciPy are broadly applicable across domains. Foundational Extends NumPy providing additional tools for array computing and provides specialized data structures, such as sparse matrices and k-dimensional trees. Performant SciPy wraps highly-optimized implementations written in low-level languages like C and C++. Enjoy the flexibility of Python with the speed of compiled code. Easy to use SciPy’s high level syntax makes it accessible and productive for programmers from any background or experience level. Open source Distributed under a liberal BSD license , SciPy is developed and maintained publicly on GitHub by a vibrant, responsive, and diverse community .

results.snippet: Buildbot - The Continuous Integration Framework
results.text: Buildbot Fork me on GitHub! Buildbot Basics Buildbot is an open-source framework for automating software build, test, and release processes. Learn more Automated Build, Test, and Release Buildbot can automate all aspects of the software development cycle: Continuous Integration, Continuous Deployment, Release Management ..and any other process you can imagine. Learn more A Framework with Batteries Included Buildbot is a framework in which you implement a system that matches your workflow and grows with your organization. Learn more Discord We have started a new Discord server for users and developers: Invite Link . Buildbot Basics Buildbot supports distributed, parallel execution of jobs across multiple platforms, flexible integration with version-control systems, extensive status reporting, and more. Buildbot in Action At its core, Buildbot is a job scheduling system: it queues jobs, executes the jobs when the required resources are available, and reports the results. Your Buildbot installation has one or more masters and a collection of workers. The masters monitor source-code repositories for changes, coordinate the activities of the workers, and report results to users and developers. Workers run on a variety of operating systems. You configure Buildbot by providing a Python configuration script to the master. This script can be very simple, configuring built-in components, but the full expressive power of Python is available. This allows dynamic generation of configuration, customized components, and anything else you can devise. The framework itself is implemented in Twisted Python, and compatible with all major operating systems. Learn More See the Buildbot Tutorial for a gentle introduction to running and configuring Buildbot. Automated Build, Test, and Release

results.text: How to Take Great Pictures of Birds, According to a Nat Geo Photographer | National Geographic ANIMALS A Beginner’s Guide to Photographing Birds Wildlife photographer and ornithologist Tim Laman shares his advice for getting started—right in your own backyard. National Geographic photographer Tim Laman has taken some incredible pictures of birds during his travels around the world. But he says aspiring wildlife photographers don't need to leave their own backyards to get creative. Photo Illustration: Annie George; Source Photos for Illustration: Tim Laman, National Geographic Image Collection By Helen Bradshaw Video by Russell Laman Published October 19, 2026 After decades traveling around the globe capturing award-winning wildlife photographs, Tim Laman is no stranger to birds. The ornithologist has shot images of birds of paradise in New Guinea, followed hornbills across Southeast Asia, and snapped pictures of cranes in Japan. Then there were the icy days spent watching penguins in Antarctica, or the time he climbed into the canopy of a kapok tree until he was eye level with the Amazon’s avian community. But one of Laman’s favorite places to shoot is still his own backyard, where chickadees flit between branches and the drama between species reveals the local pecking order. The mourning doves and house finches that cohabitate in his Massachusetts backyard aren’t the most elusive birds he’s shot—they’re far from it. But few places allow him to get as creative with bird photography as his yard. “You don't have to go to some exotic location where there are rare birds to be a good bird photographer,” he says. Laman encourages those just starting out to immerse themselves in their backyards—a place where he’s honed his own craft, experimenting with lighting and composition

There’s no playbook for female athletes over 80. So these rowers made their own—earning them a history-making berth at the Head of the Charles regatta. Much of what we assume about the 80-year-old body comes from people who stopped exercising decades ago. But these women rowers, whose average age is 80, defy those assumptions: They are poised to become the first women’s octogenarian eight to race the storied Head of the Charles regatta in October. Alan Dep, MediaNews Group, Marin Independent Journal, Getty Images By Julia Flynn Siler Published October 16, 2026 “Come on, mamacitas . You got more power!” shouts Rodrigo Rodrigues, head coach for masters rowing at the Marin Rowing Association. The women push harder against their foot stretchers and gradually their movements begin to mirror one another as they find their rhythm—sliding their seats forward, dropping their blades into the water, and unleashing a collective push that drives the boat ahead. Although Rodrigues affectionately calls them mamacitas, seven of the eight women are, in fact, abuelitas , or grandmothers. And this unusual crew of mostly silver-haired athletes is aiming to make history. On this early October morning, the women are rowing on the Corte Madera Creek, a placid waterway leading to San Francisco Bay, in their last practice with Rodrigues before flying to Boston for the Head of the Charles Regatta, one of the rowing world’s largest events. In Monarchs , photographer Jaime Rojo brings together two decades of stunning images documenting one of nature’s most extraordinary migrations, from the forests of Mexico to the fields of the American Midwest, revealing the beauty, chaos, and wonder of these remarkable butterflies. By Alexa Robles-Gil Photographs by Jaime Rojo Published October 16, 2026 In February 2004, Jaime Rojo , a young Spanish photographer, was walking uphill in Sierra Chincua, a forested mountain range in Mexico that doubles as a sanctuary for the tens of millions of monarch butterflies that migrate there each winter. As he climbed with the friends who had brought him, he began to spot monarchs along the path. Only a few at first. But the higher he went, the more he heard a sound in the background, like something whispering in the trees. Suddenly, a swarm of butterflies was flying overhead, millions of orange and black wings fluttering against the blue sky beyond. “There were so many that you could feel a slight breeze when they flew over you,” he says. Witness the breathtaking spectacle of millions of monarch butterflies in this stunning collection of photographs spanning two decades from acclaimed National Geographic photographer Jaime Rojo. results.title: The Last Stationery Shop in France Keeping a 400-Year-Old Tradition Alive | National Geographic
results.snippet: Once used for presidents, diplomats, and luxury stationers, the centuries-old art of pendulum stamping dwindled to a single master printer before finding new life in Paris.
results.text: The Last Stationery Shop in France Keeping a 400-Year-Old Tradition Alive | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE The Last Stationery Shop in France Keeping a 400-Year-Old Tradition Alive Once used for presidents, diplomats, and luxury stationers, the centuries-old art of pendulum stamping dwindled to a single master printer before finding new life in Paris. Manual pendulum stamping was once popular in the 19th century. A decreased demand a result of the digital age has led the craft to nearly disappear. Yann Garin By Lauren Paige Richeson Published October 15, 2026 Long before our messages arrived with a buzz, a letter could introduce itself by touch. Without even glimpsing the handwriting inside, the paper itself announced a family name, a profession, a crest, or a ceremony—not merely a decoration, but a declaration. In Paris, one of the most refined ways to create that impression was with timbrage au balancier , or pendulum stamping. Developed in the 19th-century world of engraving and correspondence, the technique gave calling cards, invitations, letterheads, and envelope flaps something ordinary ink could not provide: a feeling. Everything from a coat of arms to a pair of initials could rise from the page in dense color and varying depths. But as correspondence slipped from paper to pixels and luxury printing pressed faster towards mechanized processes, the manual craft began to lose the world that sustained it. By 2022, the art rested in one last pair of hands: Éric Lejeusne, France’s last manual pendulum stamper, who was preparing to retire after decades in the trade. results.title: The 'Taraia Object' Isn’t Amelia Earhart’s Plane. So What Is It? | National Geographic
results.snippet: Searchers thought that an object glinting on satellite images was the missing aviator's plane. But the reality is more quotidian.
results.text: The 'Taraia Object' Isn’t Amelia Earhart’s Plane. So What Is It? | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE The 'Taraia Object' Isn’t Amelia Earhart’s Plane. So What Is It? Searchers thought that an object glinting on satellite images was the missing aviator's plane. But the reality is more quotidian. The latest search for Amelia Earhart's plane centered on Nikumaroro, a remote atoll in the South Pacific. The island is at the center of a theory that Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan could have survived as castaways. Library of Congress, Getty Images By Rachel Hartigan Published October 19, 2026 In satellite imagery of the remote Pacific island of Nikumaroro, a mysterious object lies submerged in its lagoon—the outline of something vaguely plane-shaped. Dubbed the “ Taraia Object ” after a nearby peninsula, it has tantalized researchers who believe Amelia Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan could have ended up on the remote atoll and survived as castaways. But it’s not a plane. It’s not even metal. The strange shape is “a collection of debris,” according to the leader of the most recent attempt to discover Earhart's fate, who shared the update in a video announcement from the island A team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University—which in the 1930s had provided Earhart with funds for what was then a cutting-edge plane—broke the disappointing news after a seven-day expedition to Nikumaroro, which belongs to the nation of Kiribati and is most famously home to a population of enormous, omnivorous coconut crabs . results.title: The Kid Who Rode Into the Canyonlands and Never Came Back | National Geographic
results.snippet: Everett Ruess, a vagabond young artist and friend of Dorothea Lange, loved America's wildest vistas. Then he vanished into them forever.
results.text: The Kid Who Rode Into the Canyonlands and Never Came Back | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE The Kid Who Rode Into the Canyonlands and Never Came Back Everett Ruess, a vagabond young artist and friend of Dorothea Lange, loved America's wildest vistas. Then he vanished into them forever. Twenty-year-old Everett Ruess found a sense of the sublime in the rocky landscapes of the American Southwest—“this country suits me nearly to perfection,” he wrote once to a friend—but in 1935, he disappeared into the gulches for good. PHOTO ILLUSTRATION: AVERY WILCOX, NGM STAFF; SOURCE PHOTO (COMPOSITE): LOOK-foto, Alamy; Piotr, Adobe Stock By Rachel Hartigan Published October 19, 2026 In February 1935, government officials and media outlets across the American Southwest received the same typed letter. “Dear Sir,” it read, “Can you help us? Have you seen or heard of our son?” Everett Ruess had gone missing while trekking through the region’s remote gulches and buttes, and his parents were desperate to find him. “Everett is not inexperienced as he has lived this way in the mountains for four seasons, but not during December and January,” explained Christopher and Stella Ruess. “He may have travelled into great danger.” The recipients of the letter—postmasters and sheriffs, trading post operators and Indian agents, forest rangers and newspaper editors—all responded sympathetically to the anxious parents. But even those who’d encountered the young explorer hadn’t seen him for months. None of them knew where he was. Ruess was only 20 years old when he disappeared. For most of the previous four years, he had been traveling alone, by foot and donkey, through the Southwest’s canyonlands . results.title: Tourist Trash Has Done Weird Things to Yellowstone's Thermal Pools | National Geographic
results.snippet: For over a century, tourists have discarded objects into the park’s hydrothermal features. Park staff try to remove as much as they can. But sometimes, the litter leaves a lasting impact.
results.text: Tourist Trash Has Done Weird Things to Yellowstone's Thermal Pools | National Geographic ENVIRONMENT Tourist Trash Has Done Weird Things to Yellowstone's Thermal Pools For over a century, tourists have discarded objects into the park’s hydrothermal features. Park staff try to remove as much as they can. But sometimes, the litter leaves a lasting impact. Each year, Yellowstone National Park staff collect trash found in the park's hydrothermal areas. This year, the collection included more than 280 hats. Margery Price, National Park Service By Carolyn Wilke Published October 13, 2026 In the 1880s, a visitor to Yellowstone National Park described how the churning waters of a pool not far from Old Faithful would suck a handkerchief down and return it “nice and clean” in a few minutes. Hundreds of visitors dropped their hankies into the warm waters of the Handkerchief Pool as it was known. The pool’s trick stopped working around 1927, and in 1929, a ranger removed kerchiefs, over 100 hair pins, a horseshoe and more from the pool. Handkerchief Pool is no longer accessible by boardwalk, and tossing objects into hot springs is now illegal. But the problem of trash and debris in Yellowstone ’s features persists, as does the park’s efforts to clean it up. This year’s inventory of stuff that’s been thrown, blown or dropped into Yellowstone’s features includes some oddball objects from golf tees to hotel keys and even a tiny copy of The Vampire Diaries . “I think it’s a fascinating window into humanity,” says Margery Price, a geologist with the National Park Service. results.title: What Happens When Your New Cat Species Goes Mega-Viral? | National Geographic
results.snippet: In September, scientists revealed the tilcayo, a new wild cat. Then came donations, awards, and a few strange phone calls.
results.text: What Happens When Your New Cat Species Goes Mega-Viral? | National Geographic ANIMALS What Happens When Your New Cat Species Goes Mega-Viral? In September, scientists revealed the tilcayo, a new wild cat. Then came donations, awards, and a few strange phone calls. The discovery of the first new cat species in 100 years generated an immense amount of global attention. Scientists and its caretakers are now hopeful the interest will turn into progress for protecting its environment. Text by Jason Bittel Photographs and video by Fernando Faciole Published October 14, 2026 For seven weeks this past summer, Vicky Ossio didn’t know if any of the 1,200 rescued animals in her care would survive. Ossio is the co-founder of Senda Verde , a Bolivian wildlife sanctuary two-and-a-half hours from the capital city of La Paz. Senda Verde lies in one of the areas that was severely affected by anti-government road blockades, which cut off the flow of fuel and food in the country this summer. Each week, she needs to source nearly 500 pounds of meat to feed all the Andean bears, jaguars, and many wild cats in her care. “I would wake up and the only thing I did during the whole day is try to find food,” says Ossio. Miraculously, Senda Verde survived the blockades by buying in-season fruit from their neighbors and relying on a flock of 60 egg-laying chickens. But the experience was still fresh in Ossio’s mind when the news broke last month: Scientists had confirmed that one of the wild cats in the sanctuary was, in fact, a newly discovered species, now known as the tilcayo . Native to Bolivia, genetics revealed that the small, spotted feline had diverged from other members of the tiger cat species complex around 1.4 million years ago. results.title: As Lake Powell Dries Up, Mud Threatens Its Future | National Geographic
results.snippet: Lake Powell’s retreat is revealing a lost world covered in deep piles of sedimentary sludge. A group of adventurers and scientists are teaming up to explore its resurrected canyons, and reveal the fate of this critical reservoir.
results.text: As Lake Powell Dries Up, Mud Threatens Its Future | National Geographic ENVIRONMENT As Lake Powell Dries Up, Mud Threatens Its Future Lake Powell’s retreat is revealing a lost world covered in deep piles of sedimentary sludge. A group of adventurers and scientists are teaming up to explore its resurrected canyons, and reveal the fate of this critical reservoir. Geologic formations that have been underwater since Lake Powell was created in the 1960s are reemerging while water levels reach record lows. David McNew, Getty Images Story and video by Luke Runyon Published October 14, 2026 1:15 “Don’t stand behind me,” says Cari Johnson, as she digs a small gardening hoe into a steep slope above the Colorado River in Utah’s remote Cataract Canyon in an attempt to climb. “This is all loose.” Her warning is well-founded. As the University of Utah geology professor places one foot on her newly carved step, it gives way underneath her. “This one’s coming down,” she shouts as a basketball-sized clay boulder begins to tumble, sending up plumes of fine dust. This slope is not made of the hardened sandstone that forms the towering cliffs of the surrounding desert canyon. Johnson is studying an unstable Frankenstein’s monster composite—made up of loose sand, fine silt, cobblestone, mudstone, and clay. Much like traversing on top of an icy glacier, one wrong step on what appears to be stable ground can prove disastrous, collapsing down into steep gullies or hidden crevasses. The material is so perilous because 10 years ago, in this very spot, we would have been standing at the bottom of Lake Powell, the nation’s second-largest reservoir. results.title: What Does It Take to Move 2,000 Rhinos? | National Geographic
results.snippet: A threatened herd. An audacious plan. Inside Africa’s wildest conservation gambit.
results.text: What Does It Take to Move 2,000 Rhinos? | National Geographic ANIMALS What Does It Take to Move 2,000 Rhinos? A threatened herd. An audacious plan. Inside Africa’s wildest conservation gambit. The conservation organization African Parks bought the distressed rhino herd at a steep discount in 2023. The group plans to transport them to new homes across Africa and save the species from poachers for good. By Alex Perry Photographs by Brent Stirton Published September 23, 2026 A minute ago, Donovan Jooste’s attempt to save the rhino from extinction was going well. Jooste, 37, tanned, stocky, rarely out of a safari shirt and shorts, worked for African Parks , a nonprofit that manages wildlife reserves. Lately, his bosses had him taking care of the world’s biggest rhino herd, 2,000 southern white rhinos on a ranch outside Klerksdorp in northern South Africa, which African Parks acquired in 2023 when the animals’ original owner, a rhino-mad millionaire, ran out of money . The initial priority had been simply to ensure that the animals were properly fed. But CEO Peter Fearnhead had also been working up his own crazy rhino scheme: to divide the herd into dozens of breeding pools and sprinkle them across Africa, in an effort to create an inexhaustible, risk-diversified, poacher-protected rhino supply. To try to save the species forever. That was the grand plan, anyway. Jooste’s job was to make it work on the ground. To that end, he had been breaking the operation down into scores of translocations of 12 or so animals at a time, to reserves across the continent, in a program that will last a decade. When I joined him one morning last March, he was into his third year, preparing to move 16 rhinos to a reserve at the foot of the Waterberg mountains a day’s drive away. See more storie

results.title: Fighting to Save the Pangolin, the World’s Most Wanted Animal | National Geographic
results.snippet: Relentlessly hunted for its scales, the mysterious armored pangolin is vanishing throughout Africa. Now scientists are trying to unlock the secrets that could help save it.
results.text: Fighting to Save the Pangolin, the World’s Most Wanted Animal | National Geographic By Henry Wismayer Photographs by Marcus Westberg Published September 23, 2026 It was 4 p.m. in the forests of central Cameroon, which meant it was time to wake the pangolins . The first resident roused from slumber occupied a wooden crate positioned against the wall inside an airy clinic. The animal that emerged was as unusual as it was enchanting: around three feet long, with a low-slung body, a narrow tapering head, powerful forelimbs tipped with curved claws, a prodigious tail. A pregnant white-bellied pangolin, one of the eight recognized species, she was accustomed to this routine by now, having arrived at the Tikki Hywood Foundation ’s pangolin rescue center a week earlier. She’d been rescued from a market in the nearby town of Mbalmayo; her bruised tail suggested that she’d been caught in a snare. Too vulnerable to go outside to forage for the ants and termites that constitute her natural diet, she was being sustained with maize meal mixed with supplements, and a sprinkling of soil, which helped trigger her instinct to feed and aided her digestion. The center’s Zimbabwean founder, Lisa Hywood, held out the bowl of porridge as the animal went to work with her noodle-like tongue. To establish trust, Hywood conjured a rhythmic snorting sound from deep in her chest, mimicking the pangolin’s “chuffing” vocalizations. “It’s like they can read your energy,” she told me. “You have to succumb to them before they succumb to you.” See more stories from Africa: Earth’s Wild Home , which are featured in the October 2026 issue of National Geographic magazine. results.title: There's a New 'Blue Zone'—And It Holds Clues to Women's Longevity | National Geographic
results.snippet: The idyllic village is one of the most "extraordinary" spots on the globe for making it to 100.
results.text: There's a New 'Blue Zone'—And It Holds Clues to Women's Longevity | National Geographic Premium HEALTH There's a New Blue Zone—And It Holds Clues to Women's Longevity The idyllic village is one of the most "extraordinary" spots on the globe for making it to 100. A National Geographic project led by longevity researcher Dan Buettner has identified a new 'blue zone'—a geographic region where residents 70 and older have exceptional survival—centered on the mountainous Sardinian village of Bolotana. There, junk food is a foreign concept and female life expectancy is particularly high. By Jessica Roy Photographs by Marisa Montibeller Published October 5, 2026 A diet rich in bacon, blueberries, and chocolate. Having a “lighthearted spirit” and a positive attitude. Forty cigarettes a day . Ask a centenarian about the key to longevity, and each will have a different response. Though blueberries certainly won’t hurt (the cigarettes might), the real answer to the question of how to live a long, healthy life might actually be hidden along the slopes of the Marghine mountains, in a tiny town on Sardinia called Bolotana. Surrounded by woodlands and dotted with fresh springs, Bolotana is a small village of around 2,262 people, 10 of whom are at least 100 years old. This prevalence of centenarians—about 442 per 100,000 residents—is roughly 10 times the Sardinian average and 11 times the U.S. average. Those numbers have made Bolotana of particular interest to National Geographic Explorer and longtime longevity researcher Dan Buettner, who is best known for his work on blue zones , geographic regions in which residents 70 and older have exceptional survival and longevity odds. results.title: A Kelvin Wave Is Pulsing Up the West Coast. Here’s What to Expect. | National Geographic
results.snippet: Scientists say the Kelvin wave could be dangerous for people—and deadly for wildlife—as it travels up the California coast.
results.text: A Kelvin Wave Is Pulsing Up the West Coast. Here’s What to Expect. | National Geographic ENVIRONMENT A Pacific 'Blob' Is Pulsing Up the West Coast. Here's What's to Expect. Scientists say the Kelvin wave could be dangerous for people—and deadly for wildlife—as it travels up the California coast. Last month, around 20 homes were evacuated in Long Beach, California after heavy surf caused flooding. A blob of warm water known as a Kelvin wave is exacerbating coastal flooding caused by warmer waters, storms, and rising seas. Mario Tama, Getty Images By Ruby Mellen Published October 6, 2026 Sea levels across the west coasts of the Americas are rising after a massive bulge of water, driven by wind changes and a warmer ocean, inched its way east along the equator and along the coasts. The phenomenon, called a Kelvin wave, has officials bracing for storm surges, erosion, and transformations in marine life. Networks of satellites and buoys across the ocean have been tracking the pulse of water, which arrived on Southern California’s coast last week and will continue north. Experts say that while the wave itself isn’t especially damaging to property or infrastructure along the coast, it can worsen the damage already being inflicted by an increase in storms, climate change-driven sea-level rise, and record-high ocean temperatures, which cause water to expand. It’s also one of the major signs that the much-anticipated super El Niño born in the equatorial Pacific Ocean has made it to North and South America. "It's an important part of the development and evolution of El Niño," says Michael Jacox, a research oceanographer at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. “You can see the link from the tropical ocean all the way to the West Coast,” he adds. results.title: 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster | National Geographic
results.snippet: This month brings two meteor showers, an eerie orange-tinted full moon, and one of the year’s last chances to glimpse the Milky Way’s luminous core.
results.text: 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster | National Geographic SCIENCE NIGHT SKY GUIDE 8 Night Sky Events to See in October, From Fiery Meteors to a Vanishing Star Cluster This month brings two meteor showers, an eerie orange-tinted full moon, and one of the year’s last chances to glimpse the Milky Way’s luminous core. A long-exposure photograph captures stars appearing to streak across the night sky above Joshua Tree National Park in California. By Stephanie Vermillion Photographs by Sean Parker Published September 24, 2026 With streaking meteors and exceptional planet sightings, October provides plenty of reasons to stay up and stargaze. Two meteor showers punctuate the month: The Draconids peak beneath the dark skies of a nearly new moon, while the Orionids arrive later in October. Saturn also reaches opposition, when the planet appears at its biggest and brightest, creating an excellent opportunity to glimpse its famed rings. Meteor showers—and, now that autumn has arrived, the northern lights —are best viewed beneath dark skies away from light pollution . But all is not lost for urban sky-watchers; some of the month’s top spectacles, including planet sightings, are visible through city lights. You just need to know when and where to look. Saturn at opposition — October 4 Saturn will reach its closest point to Earth, known as its opposition, around 8 a.m. ET on Oct. 4. The days leading up to and following it are also a great time to spot the planet’s famed rings. To spy the planet, look to the south-southeast around 11 p.m.; the view improves for the next few hours as Saturn climbs higher in the sky. ( How to photograph the stars using your phone .) You’ll need at least a small backyard telescope or high-powered binoculars

results.title: How a Nat Geo Photographer Captured Iconic Photos of Big Cats | National Geographic
results.snippet: Wildlife photographer Steve Winter has been stalked by tigers and chased by a rhino—all in pursuit of these stunning images featured in his new retrospective book with the author Sharon Guynup.
results.text: How a Nat Geo Photographer Captured Iconic Photos of Big Cats | National Geographic ANIMALS How a Nat Geo Photographer Captured Iconic Photos of Big Cats Wildlife photographer Steve Winter has been stalked by tigers and chased by a rhino—all in pursuit of these stunning images featured in his new retrospective book with the author Sharon Guynup. In Big Cats , Steve Winter and journalist Sharon Guynup chronicle the world’s mightiest felids—lions, and tigers, and jaguars, oh my—and show how their work has helped protect and conserve these awe-inspiring species. By Rachel Nuwer Photographs by Steve Winter Published October 6, 2026 Big cats are masters of staying hidden, a skill honed by millions of years of evolution. Today, they have another reason to remain out of sight: humans. Yet National Geographic contributing photographer Steve Winter has built a career capturing tigers, lions, jaguars, snow leopards, and cougars in moments few people would ever witness. Making those images requires meticulous planning, technical ingenuity, patience, and artistic instinct—along with a fair amount of luck. Come face-to-face with lions, tigers, and more in this gorgeous retrospective collection of narrated images from renowned National Geographic photographer, Steve Winter. BUY THE BOOK NOW In Big Cats , a new retrospective created with environmental journalist Sharon Guynup, Winter brings together his photographs from decades in the field, like the image above of a Sumatran tiger. results.text: Dian Fossey's Original Story on Life With the Gorillas | National Geographic Premium ANIMALS FROM THE VAULT Dian Fossey's Original Story on Life With the Gorillas Before Dian Fossey met her tragic fate, she came face to face with some of humankind’s closest nonhuman relatives. Mark Thiessen By Dian Fossey Photographs by Robert M. Campbell Published October 1, 2026 This story originally published in the January 1970 issue of National Geographic magazine. This feature is presented as originally created and may contain stereotypes or negative depictions. See more digitized stories from our archives here . For the past three years I have spent most of my days with wild mountain gorillas . Their home, and mine, has been the misty wooded slopes of the Virunga range, eight lofty volcanoes—the highest is 14,787 feet—shared by three African nations, Rwanda, Uganda , and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Cover of the January 1970 National Geographic Magazine. During this time I have become well acquainted with many of the gorillas, and they with me. They roam the mountain slopes and saddles in groups, and several groups now accept my presence almost as a member. I can approach to within a few feet of them, and some, especially the juveniles and young adults, have come even closer, picked up my camera strap, and examined the buckle on my knapsack. One has even played with the laces on my boots, though I have a feeling that he did not suspect that the boots were, in fact, connected with me. I know the gorillas as individuals, each with his own traits and personality, and, mainly for identification in my hundreds of pages of notes, I have given many of them names: Rafiki, Uncle Bert, Icarus, and so on. The Hidden Toll of Extreme Heat on Pregnancy With global temperatures on the rise, researchers are confronting an increasingly urgent problem: the impact of extreme heat on expectant mothers and their babies. results.snippet: Nimble and fast, Spitfire PR planes ran vital photo missions for Allied forces.
results.text: The Reconnaissance Plane That Helped Win World War II | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE The Reconnaissance Plane That Helped Win World War II Nimble and fast, Spitfire PR planes ran vital photo missions for Allied forces. A Supermarine Spitfire Mark IIA flies over the coast of Britain in this colorized version of the original 1941 photograph. Royal Air Force official photographer, Imperial War Museums via Getty Images By John Lancaster Published September 25, 2026 Alone and unarmed, British Royal Air Force (RAF) pilot Alastair “Sandy” Gunn took off from Wick air base in northern Scotland in a Supermarine Spitfire PR.IV, a camera-equipped version of the storied single-engine fighter plane. His destination was a fjord near Trondheim on the Norwegian coast, where the German battleship Tirpitz had taken refuge. Prime Minister Winston Churchill was deeply concerned about the Tirpitz and the threat it posed to Allied convoys carrying tanks, aircraft, and other weaponry—along with more mundane supplies such as boots and telephone wire—to Soviet ports on the Arctic Ocean, a hazardous voyage of up to 2,500 miles that skirted Norway’s northern coast. Gunn’s mission was to locate the ship, photograph it, and return to Scotland with the film—a 1,200-mile round-trip journey over frigid waters and enemy territory. He never made it back. Somewhere above the snow-covered mountains near Trondheim, two Messerschmitt Bf 109 fighters intercepted his defenseless Spitfire and riddled it with machine-gun and cannon fire. He bailed out of his burning airplane and parachuted to the ground, only to be captured a few days later. results.text: Ann Arbor, Michigan, Is a Charming College Town That Delivers Big-City Culture | National Geographic TRAVEL COLLEGE TOWNS Ann Arbor, Michigan, Is a Charming College Town That Delivers Big-City Culture Best known for Big Ten sports, this small city offers a surprising breadth of experiences, including big-time art, music, and nature. The Michigan Theater, a historic Ann Arbor movie palace opened in 1927, hosts indie flicks, stage plays, and live concerts. Wangkun Jia, Shutterstock By Brooke Sabin Published September 24, 2026 When the playwright Arthur Miller first set foot in Ann Arbor in 1934 as an eager university student, he recalled later in an appreciative piece for Holiday magazine, “I fell in love with the place, groggy as I was from the bus ride.” Many visitors to this compact Midwestern town do, finding themselves drawn to its outsize intellectual vigor and varied cultural, culinary, and outdoor experiences. Founded in 1824, Ann Arbor—or A2, as it’s sometimes called—sits along the Huron River in southeast Michigan , with a lively downtown of 19th and early 20th century brick facades that house restaurants, coffee shops, boutiques—and more than a few surprises. (Look out for the whimsical fairy doors hidden among the buildings.) Another of the city’s nicknames, Tree Town, testifies to its abundant greenery. But Ann Arbor is better known for another color. When the University of Michigan Wolverines take on their rivals, cries of “Go Blue!” echo across town. Indeed, U of M, considered one of America’s “Public Ivies,” shapes much of Ann Arbor’s culture and daily life, especially when students arrive in late summer and the year-round population of 123,000 swells by 50,000. results.text: Where to Take a Day Trip From Amsterdam | National Geographic TRAVEL Where to Take a Day Trip From Amsterdam The heavily touristed city has quick and easy access to a number of charming and diverse day trips. Just a quick train ride from Amsterdam will bring you to Rotterdam and its fascinating array of architecture. fotolupa, Adobe Stock By Chadner Navarro Published October 4, 2026 Tens of millions of visitors throng the canal-ringed neighborhoods of Amsterdam every year, savoring meals at its Michelin-starred restaurants and soaking up the culture at its world-class museums. But the Netherlands is more than just its biggest and most well-known city. Adding a quick day-trip to nearby destinations such as Rotterdam , Utrecht , and Zandvoort can make for a more dynamic overall visit. In Rotterdam, learn about the port that helped create one of the most diverse cities on the continent. In Utrecht, a surprising take on Dutch canal culture awaits. And Zandvoort’s nine-kilometer beach makes a case for an unexpected Eurosummer. Bonus: thanks to the country’s dependable train system, all three are less than 45 minutes away from Amsterdam’s central station. ( How to Spend the Perfect Day Finding Amsterdam's Alternative Side ) Rotterdam The Netherland’s second largest city with a population just shy of 675,000, Rotterdam has lived many lives: First as a fishing village in the 13th century and then as one of the most important maritime hubs in Europe. As the continent’s largest, the port of Rotterdam was the starting point of many journeys to the New World, both in terms of trade and immigration. The man took the animal home, believing it to be a domestic breed. But after about a year of living with the clearly wild animal, he realized it would be better off at a sanctuary. As the lead scientist and founder of the Bolivian Felids Research Program ( Programa de Investigación de Félidos Bolivia ), Nogales-Ascarrunz was intrigued. The animal had a small, scrunched-up face, short and round ears, and long whiskers. It was, indeed, too small to be a housecat, and, most notably, it was covered in leopard-like spots. So she went to visit the creature at the Senda Verde wildlife sanctuary on the subtropical flank of the Bolivian Andes. “I took a hundred pictures of it,” remembers Nogales-Ascarrunz. “I was so fascinated.” What she couldn’t know at the time was that this curious cat had a secret. It would become the first new species of felid (i.e. the cat family) discovered in over 100 years, according to a study published today in the journal Current Biology . Jodi Cobb, National Geographic Image Collection By Domonique Tolliver Published August 25, 2026 Dolly Parton—whose unmistakable voice and extraordinary songwriting made her one of the most recognizable figures in American culture—has died at 80 years old, as confirmed in a video message from her family. For more than six decades, the “Queen of Country” wove stories of heartbreak, ambition, and home into songs shared across generations. Her songwriting formed a tapestry of the beauty and hardships of life in Appalachia, where she spent her childhood before pursuing her music career in Nashville. Parton was a philanthropic force. She donated hundreds of millions of dollars over her lifetime and was recognized with the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy in 2022. Her work in literacy is a defining aspect of her legacy, connecting millions of children with free books through her Imagination Library and giving the gift of education through her Dollywood Foundation. She also gave $1 million to fund COVID-19 research and supported the development of the Moderna mRNA vaccine. Parton also did her part in protecting our planet. results.snippet: Warm El Niño waters are driving an increase in stingray injuries. These labs are devoted to understanding what’s going on under the surface.
results.text: How This Zombie Foot is Helping Scientists Fight Stingray Strikes | National Geographic ANIMALS How This Zombie Foot is Helping Scientists Fight Stingray Strikes Warm El Niño waters are driving an increase in stingray injuries. These labs are devoted to understanding what’s going on under the surface. To trigger a sting, scientists at the STABB Lab gently press a fake foot down onto a stingray. Ben Perlman, STABB Lab By Katharine Gammon Published October 15, 2026 Stingrays regularly cruise the California coastline, but this year they are so abundant they blanket the sea floor like a leathery carpet. That’s because El Niño has brought warmer waters to the West Coast's beaches. California’s Bolsa Chica and Huntington State Beaches have treated over 3,500 injuries so far this year—roughly twice the total for all of 2025. “Stingray injuries spike with water temperature and especially during El Niño years,” says Chris Lowe, who leads California State University, Long Beach’s Shark Lab. His research team is studying the increase in Southern California’s injury rates over the last four years. “Based on our discussions with lifeguards, injury reports are up for this year at this time,” he says. Beachgoers, who are similarly descending upon warmer-than-average beaches, have been getting pierced by a small species of stingray called a round ray. "Round rays like nice, warm, calm water and so do humans,” says Ben Perlman, who runs the STABB (Stingray and Butterfly Biomechanics) Lab, also at California State University, Long Beach. With higher ocean temperatures due to El Niño, “more people are flocking to the beach for all the right reasons, and that's exactly where the round rays are."
